announcements.text: Northrop Grumman Systems Corp., Aerospace Systems. Melbourne, Florida, is awarded a not-to-exceed $1,196,000,000 cost, no fee undefinitized contract for the production, delivery, and associated support for three E-2D Advanced Hawkeye Block II aircraft for the Navy. Work will be performed in Melbourne, Florida (29.88%); St. Augustine, Florida (17.68%); Liverpool, New York (13.85%); Indianapolis, Indiana (4.95%); Largo, Florida (3.66%); San Leandro, California (2.52%); Woodland Hills, California (2.42%); Aire-sur-l’Adour, France (2.09%); Rolling Meadows, Illinois (1.72%); Wimborne Minster, Dorset, United Kingdom (0.01%); and various locations within the continental U.S. (21.22%), and is expected to be completed in December 2031. Fiscal 2026 aircraft procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $583,394,000 will be obligated at the time of award. This contract was not competed in accordance with 10 U.S. Code 2304(c)(1). Naval Air Systems Command, Patuxent River, Maryland, is the contracting activity (N0001926C1017).

Raytheon, Tucson, Arizona, is awarded an $18,977,361 cost-plus-fixed-fee modification to previously awarded contract (N00024-26-C-5434) for technical and design agent engineering in support of the Evolved SeaSparrow Missile and NATO SeaSparrow Missile Systems programs. Work will be performed in Tucson, Arizona (85%); and Portsmouth, Rhode Island (15%), and is expected to be completed by December 2030. This modification combines purchases for the U.S. Navy (36%) and the governments of Australia, Belgium, Canada, Denmark, Germany, Greece, Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Spain, Türkiye (under Memorandum of Agreements (63%)); and Japan (under Foreign Military Sales (FMS) cases (1%)). Fiscal 2025 other customer funds in the amount of $7,697,880 (36%); fiscal 2026 other customer funds in the amount of $5,295,484 (24%); fiscal 2026 weapons procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $ 2,429,221 (11%); fiscal 2025 operations and maintenance (Navy) funds in the amount of $1,766,007 (8%); fiscal 2026 other procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $1,736,477 (8%); fiscal 2025 weapons procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $1,122,366 (5%); fiscal 2024 weapons procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $530,573 (2%); fiscal 2024 other customer funds in the amount of $433,289 (2%); fiscal 2026 FMS Japan funds in the amount of $251,165 (1%); fiscal 2022 other customer funds in the amount of $150,000 (1%); fiscal 2024 other procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $111,656 (1%); and fiscal 2023 other customer funds in the amount of $83,000 (<1%); fiscal 2025 other procurement (Navy) $20,569 (<1%) will be obligated at time of award, of which $642,229 will expire at the end of the current fiscal year. The Naval Sea Systems Command, Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity.

The Boeing Co., St. Louis, Missouri, is being awarded $18,798,154 for a not-to-exceed, firm-fixed-price delivery order (N00383-26-F-YY1N) for the repair of 27 distributed targeting processor network in support of the F-18 aircraft. The delivery order does not include an option period. Work will be performed in St. Louis, Missouri (50%); and Malabar, Florida (50%), and work is expected to be completed by March 2028. Fiscal 2026 working capital funds (Navy) in the amount of $9,211,095 will be obligated at the time of award as an undefinitized contract action and the funds do not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. Subsequent task orders will be funded with appropriate fiscal year working capital funds (Navy). One company was solicited for this sole-source requirement pursuant to the authority set forth in 10 U.S. Code 3204(a)(1), with one offer received. Naval Supply Systems Command Weapon Systems Support, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, is the contracting activity.

NewVac LLC,* Chatsworth, California, is awarded a $17,874,470 firm-fixed-price modification to previously awarded contract (N6339422C0009) to exercise options for the manufacture, assembly, test, and delivery of vertical launching system module cables, module deck and hatch cable set, MK 41 Mod 47 ancillary cable set, extender cable set, and B/L VII DDG 51-class AEGIS modernization cable set. This contract combines purchases for the Navy (52%); and the governments of Spain (24%), Netherlands (21%), and Germany (3%), under the Foreign Military Sales (FMS) Program. Work will be performed in Chatsworth, California, and is expected to be completed by September 2027. Fiscal 2026 shipbuilding and conversion (Navy) funds in the amount of 9,060,995 (51%); FMS (Spain) funds in the amount of $4,296,806 (24%); FMS (Netherlands) funds in the amount of $3,698,748 (21%); FMS (Germany) funds in the amount of $618,220 (3%); and fiscal 2026 other procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $199,701 (1%), will be obligated at time of award and will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. Naval Surface Warfare Center Port Hueneme Division, Port Hueneme, California, is the contracting activity.

CORRECTION: The contract announced on July 21, 2026, for The Raytheon Co., Tucson, Arizona, for $49,720,000 was announced with the wrong amount. The correct amount is $49,719,999. Naval Supply Systems Command, Weapon Systems Support, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, is the contracting activity.

Laboratory Corp. of America, Burlington, North Carolina, was awarded $364,702,439 for a single-award, indefinite delivery/indefinite quantity contract utilizing firm-fixed-price task orders to provide the Defense Health Agency with commercial clinical reference laboratory testing services across both the continental United States and outside the continental United States. This competitive, non-personal services contract will support military beneficiaries worldwide by processing vital diagnostic laboratory tests that military medical treatment facilities currently lack the capability or capacity to execute in-house. This strategic sourcing initiative was competitively solicited under solicitation number HT001526RE001, which was posted to SAM.gov on May 12, 2026, and closed on June 1, 2026. The contract features a five-year base period followed by a five-year option period, establishing a worldwide performance location with an ultimate completion date of July 9, 2036. No fiscal 2026 operations and maintenance funds are being obligated at time of award. The Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity, Enterprise Medical Services Contracting Division, San Antonio, Texas, is the contracting activity.

Synensys LLC, Peachtree, Georgia, is awarded $9,391,875 for a firm-fixed price option modification (P00002) to a previously awarded contract (HT001125C0076) for Defense Health Agency (DHA) Deputy Assistant Director - Medical Affairs Patient Safety Program for military medical treatment facilities services. The contract encompasses patient safety personnel at numerous military hospitals and clinics coupled with training materials to foster a workplace-based safety cultural transformation, guided by experts in patient safety at DHA. Services include expertise and experience required by patient safety specialists, patient safety assistant coordinators, and patient safety data analysts at both inpatient and outpatient facilities. Fiscal 2026 operations and maintenance funds are obligated to exercise and fully fund Option One for 12 months from Aug. 1, 2026, to July 31, 2027. The places of performance are military hospitals and clinics inside and outside the continental U.S. DHA, Professional Services Contracting Division, Falls Church, Virginia, is the contracting activity.

Parsons Government Services Inc., Centreville, Virginia (W91278-26-D-A035); Tetra Tech Inc., Pasadena, California (W91278-26-D-A036); Jacobs Government Services Co., Arlington, Virginia (W91278-26-D-A037); HDR Engineering Inc., Omaha, Nebraska (W91278-26-D-A038); Alpha Facilities Solutions LLC,* San Antonio, Texas (W91278-26-D-A039); Stantec GS Inc., Charlottesville, Virginia (W91278-26-D-A040); and WSP USA Inc., Washington, D.C. (W91278-26-D-A041), will compete for each order of the $249,000,000 firm-fixed-price contract for architect-engineer services. Bids were solicited via the internet with 13 received. Work locations and funding will be determined with each order, with an estimated completion date of July 21, 2031. U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Mobile, Alabama, is the contracting activity.

Northrop Grumman Systems Corp., McLean, Virginia, was awarded a $27,888,512 modification (PZ0004) to contract W31P4Q-26-C-0011 to definitize an undefinitized contract action for engineering support, integrated product support, field service representative support, and training and training material support software products. One bid was solicited with one received. Work will be performed in McLean, Virginia, with an estimated completion date of Jan. 21, 2029. Fiscal 2026 aircraft procurement, Army funds in the amount of $9,317,073 were obligated at the time of the award. Army Contracting Command, Redstone Arsenal, Alabama, is the contracting activity.

Torch Technologies Inc., Huntsville, Alabama, was awarded a $12,395,054 modification (P00286) to contract W31P4Q-21-F-0038, for hardware in the loop systems of systems development, integration and testing support. The modification brings the total cumulative face value of the contract to $659,292,704. Bids were solicited via the internet with three received. Work locations and funding will be determined with each order, with an estimated completion date of July 22, 2027. Army Contracting Command, Redstone Arsenal, Alabama, is the contracting activity.

Hensel Phelps Construction Co., Orlando, Florida, was awarded a $10,000,000 modification (P00032) to contract W91278-22-C-0008 for an equitable adjustment to settle material, equipment and labor costs, providing a partial payment so construction can proceed while final schedule delays and costs are definitized. One bid was solicited with one received. Work will be performed in Panama City, Florida, with an estimated completion date of Dec. 12, 2026. Fiscal 2025 military construction, Air Force funds in the amount of $10,000,000 were obligated at the time of the award. U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Mobile, Alabama, is the contracting activity.

Frank M. Gargiulo & Son Inc.,* Hillside, New Jersey, has been awarded a maximum $202,286,703 fixed-price with economic-price-adjustment, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for fresh fruits and vegetables. This was a competitive acquisition with four responses received. This is a five-year contract with no option periods. Locations of performance are Maryland, Delaware, and Washington, D.C., with a July 19, 2031, ordering period end date. Using customers are Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, Coast Guard, and Department of Agriculture. Type of appropriation is fiscal 2026 through 2031 defense working capital funds. The contracting agency is Defense Logistics Agency Troop Support, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania (SPE300-26-D-P451).

Spiral Solutions and Technologies Inc., Bellevue, Nebraska, has been awarded a maximum $49,141,033 firm-fixed-price level of effort contract for joint exercise, training, assessment and related support. This contract provides for planning, development, execution, and analysis of joint exercises for U.S. Strategic Command. Work will be performed at Offutt Air Force Base, Nebraska, and is expected to be completed by Aug. 5, 2031. This contract was a competitive acquisition, and four offers were received. Fiscal 2026 operation and maintenance funds in the amount of $7,407,400 are being obligated at time of award. The 55th Contracting Squadron, Offutt AFB, Nebraska, is the contracting activity (FA4600-26-F-0050).

Sigmatech Inc., Huntsville, Alabama, has been awarded a $49,032,775 firm-fixed-price contract for systems engineering and technical assistance services. This contract provides for technical, system analysis, programmatic, requirements, and analytical support for Space Systems Delta 80, Directorate, Operations Integration and Directorate, Servicing, Mobility, and Logistics. Work will be performed at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Florida; and Peterson Space Force Base, Colorado, and is expected to be completed by March 12, 2032. This contract was a competitive acquisition, and one offer was received. Fiscal 2026 procurement funds in the amount of $4,082,732; and fiscal 2026 research, development, test and evaluation funds in the amount of $536,453 are being obligated at time of award. The 45th Contracting Squadron, Patrick SFB, Florida, is the contracting activity (FA2521-26-F-0273).

Deloitte Consulting LLP, Arlington, Virginia, has been awarded a $20,527,492 firm-fixed-price modification (P00025) to a previously awarded contract (FA7014-24-F-0461) for technical support services. The modification brings the total cumulative face value of the contract to $56,372,569 from $35,845,078. Work will be performed in Washington, D.C., and is expected to be completed Sept. 29, 2029. Fiscal 2026 operations and maintenance funds in the amount of $7,079,222 are being obligated at the time of award. The Air Force District of Washington Contracting Directorate, Joint Base Andrews, Maryland, is the contracting activity.
